section_title: What does Moab miss when it dismisses Judah as just another nation?

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 8 This is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Because Moab and Seir said, “Look, the house of Judah is like all the other nations,” 9 therefore I will indeed expose the flank of Moab beginning with its frontier cities—Beth-jeshimoth, Baal-meon, and Kiriathaim—the glory of the land. 10 I will give it along with the Ammonites as a possession to the people of the East, so that the Ammonites will no longer be remembered among the nations. 11 So I will execute judgments on Moab, and they will know that I am the LORD.’

context_lines: Moab and Seir say that Judah is like all the other nations. In the setting of Judah’s fall, that dismissal denies that its relationship with the Lord makes any difference.
The Lord answers by announcing the exposure of Moab’s flank, beginning with the named frontier cities. The land’s glory will not secure it against judgment.
Moab’s fate is placed beside Ammon’s: the land will be given to the people from the East. The closing purpose answers the original dismissal. Moab will know the Lord through His judgments.
common_interpretation_lines: [Wesley](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/ezekiel/25.htm) understands the taunt as denying that Judah is a people specially chosen by God. [Henry](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/mhc/ezekiel/25.htm) emphasizes the danger of relying on defenses other than the Lord’s power and promise.
The passage distinguishes Judah’s relationship with God without denying its guilt. Judah’s defeat is not proof that the Lord has no claim on it or no authority over its neighbors.
god_plan_lines: [Jeremiah 48:46–47](https://biblehub.com/bsb/jeremiah/48.htm) also announces captivity for Moab, then promises that the Lord will restore Moab from captivity in the latter days. That promise adds something this short judgment does not state.
The wider picture leaves room for the Lord’s mercy beyond Israel’s borders. Mercy does not erase the wrong being judged, but judgment does not exhaust what the Lord promises.
